title: Definition of hallmarking
content: Hallmarking is the accurate determination and official recording of the proportionate content of precious metal in precious-metal articles.

title: Precious metals currently covered
content: BIS states that gold and silver are the two precious metals currently brought under the hallmarking framework in India.

title: IS 1417:2016
content: BIS identifies IS 1417:2016 as the standard for gold and gold alloys, jewellery/artefacts, fineness and marking specification.

title: IS 2112:2014
content: BIS identifies IS 2112:2014 as the standard for silver and silver alloys, jewellery/artefacts, fineness and marking specification.

title: IS 15820:2009
content: BIS identifies IS 15820:2009 as the general requirements standard for establishment and operation of Assaying and Hallmarking Centres.

title: IS 1418:2009
content: BIS identifies IS 1418:2009 as the method for determination of gold in bullion, alloys and jewellery/artefacts by cupellation (fire assay).

title: IS 2113:2014
content: BIS identifies IS 2113:2014 as an assaying method standard for silver and silver alloys.

title: HUID format
content: HUID is a six-digit alphanumeric number, unique for each hallmarked item and traceable.

title: Current three-mark hallmark
content: Since introduction of HUID on 1 July 2021, BIS states that hallmark consists of BIS logo, purity in caratage/fineness and six-digit alphanumeric HUID.

title: Hallmarking charges
content: BIS states hallmarking charges are paid per article irrespective of article weight.

title: Invoice requirements
content: BIS consumer FAQ states the bill/invoice should include article description, net precious-metal weight, purity in carat/fineness and hallmarking charges.

title: Pairs of jewellery
content: BIS consumer FAQ states each article in a pair should have hallmarking and fineness details should be checked on each article.

title: Detachable jewellery parts
content: BIS consumer FAQ states each detachable part of jewellery should have a hallmark.

title: Retail display requirements
content: BIS guidance states registered/certified jewellers should display BIS signage, certificate, hallmark information and a minimum 10X magnifying glass for customer inspection.

title: Old jewellery FAQ
content: BIS's common-consumer FAQ states that old jewellery cannot be hallmarked under the cited FAQ response.

title: Hallmark fee scope
content: BIS consumer FAQ states hallmarking charges do not include making charges or wastage charges.

title: Refinery applicant eligibility

title: Refinery prerequisites
content: BIS lists in-house manufacturing and testing capability and laboratory accreditation by NABL or LBMA as prerequisites.

title: Refinery licence scope
content: BIS states refinery/mint licence scope covers gold bullion or gold coin, fineness 999 or 995, and declared design/weight, with no negative tolerance on declared weight.

title: Refinery licence validity
content: BIS states refinery/mint licence is initially valid for one year and may be renewed for a maximum period of two years.

title: Refinery marking fee
content: BIS states minimum annual marking fee is ₹48,000 for large-scale gold refineries and ₹38,400 for MSME units, with production-based marking fee of ₹50 per unit where one unit equals 1 kg.

title: How much does BIS product testing cost?
content: BIS testing cost is not one universal fixed amount. The applicable laboratory testing charge depends on the product, applicable Indian Standard, laboratory, test scope and the tests required. The RAG must retrieve the applicable laboratory scope and current fee information rather than quote a generic amount.

title: Where can I find the current testing charge for a BIS test?
content: Current testing charges should be taken from the applicable BIS LIMS laboratory scope/fee information or the authoritative BIS document for that test. The answer should identify the laboratory and applicable standard/test before quoting an amount.

title: Does every BIS-recognized laboratory charge the same testing fee?
content: Do not assume that all BIS-recognized laboratories charge the same amount. Fees must be checked against the applicable laboratory and its current published scope/charge information.

title: Can I know the testing cost before sending my product to a laboratory?
content: Yes, where the laboratory publishes applicable charges, the current BIS LIMS scope/fee information can be used to identify the relevant test and charge. The exact amount should be quoted only when supported by current authoritative laboratory data.

title: What information is needed to estimate laboratory testing cost?
content: At minimum, identify the product, applicable Indian Standard, required test or test group, and the laboratory whose scope is being considered. Different tests and laboratories can have different charges.

title: Can the BIS assistant give me a testing fee for my product?
content: It should give a testing fee only when the current authoritative laboratory record supports the amount and identifies the relevant standard/test. If the current fee is unavailable, it should say that the fee could not be verified instead of estimating it.

title: What is the difference between BIS product certification fees and laboratory testing charges?
content: They are different categories of cost. A laboratory may charge for testing, while BIS certification involves its own applicable certification, application, inspection or other prescribed charges. The assistant should retrieve each applicable fee separately rather than combine them into one unsupported total.

title: Will testing cost be the same for every product under BIS certification?
content: No universal amount should be assumed. Testing requirements and applicable charges depend on the product, applicable Indian Standard, tests and laboratory scope.

title: How do I find a laboratory that can test my product?
content: Identify the applicable Indian Standard and then use the BIS LIMS laboratory directory and scope records to find laboratories whose published scope includes the required standard/test.

title: Can I use any laboratory for BIS-required testing?
content: Not automatically. The applicable certification scheme or requirement determines what laboratory status is acceptable. The assistant should verify the relevant BIS requirement and the laboratory's current recognized/empanelled status and scope.

title: What if the laboratory fee is not available online?
content: The assistant should state that the current fee could not be verified from the authoritative source. It should not infer a fee from another laboratory or from an old record.

title: Can the same test have different charges at different laboratories?
content: A generic single charge should not be assumed. Current laboratory-specific fee information should be checked for the required test and standard.

title: How much does jewellery purity testing cost under BIS hallmarking?
content: The BIS Hallmarking FAQ states that a consumer can get jewellery tested at a recognized Assaying & Hallmarking Centre and identifies a ₹200 fire-assay testing charge in the stated context. The assistant should cite the current BIS FAQ when giving this amount.

title: Can a consumer test jewellery at a BIS-recognized Assaying & Hallmarking Centre?
content: Yes. BIS consumer guidance states that consumers can get jewellery tested at a BIS-recognized Assaying & Hallmarking Centre, subject to the applicable procedure and report requirements.

title: What should I ask a laboratory before sending a sample?
content: Confirm the applicable Indian Standard/test, whether the laboratory's current BIS scope covers the required test, the current testing charge, sample requirements, turnaround information where published, and the required report format.

title: Why should the BIS assistant avoid giving an estimated laboratory fee?
content: A guessed fee can be wrong because laboratory charges are tied to the specific test, standard, laboratory and current fee schedule. The assistant should provide only an amount supported by current authoritative evidence.

title: What if I only know my product name but not the Indian Standard?
content: First identify the applicable Indian Standard from authoritative BIS product/standard information. Laboratory selection and testing cost should be determined only after the relevant standard and test requirements are established.

title: Does a laboratory's published scope prove that every test is currently available?
content: The assistant should use the current BIS LIMS scope and status information and should not infer availability beyond what the authoritative record states.

title: Can I ask for a complete testing-cost estimate?
content: Yes, but the estimate must be assembled from verified applicable costs. The assistant should distinguish laboratory testing charges from BIS certification fees and clearly identify any cost that could not be verified.

title: What should the assistant say if there is no current fee for my required test?
content: It should explicitly state that the current fee could not be verified from the authoritative BIS source and provide the relevant laboratory or source page for further verification, rather than inventing a number.
